about: Graded benchmark for the S2.1 place-name resolver. Intended answers are written down HERE, before the resolver is run, because four consecutive Codex passes found over-corrections that the five-query benchmark could not see. See docs/plans/2026-11-03-phase1-plan.md S2.1.

grading.note: Location grading uses ONLY the twelve hand-chosen spot-check reference points, which are justified independently of this resolver and are not POI centroids. The threshold is deliberately coarse: it separates 'the same place' from 'somewhere else entirely'. Queries with no justified reference carry property assertions instead. Adding more reference coordinates needs an independent source, not my recollection; that is a stated gap, not a thing to fill in by guessing.

queries.intent: the hospital campus in Chapel Hill
queries.basis: justified reference point; the original decision-D4 benchmark query that Nominatim resolved to Morganton, 180 km away Tightened after pass-14 M3: an unrelated non-stop leader passed while another candidate supplied the nearby point.

queries.intent: same, with the locality typed as a suffix
queries.basis: a correct locality must not make a correct answer worse

queries.intent: same, with region noise
queries.basis: strip_region_noise must remove 'NC' without touching the name

queries.intent: the hospital, not the bus platform named after it
queries.basis: pass-10 H1: this resolved CONFIDENTLY to a bus platform, and pass-12 H4 made it abstain. The requirement is the abstention plus a real place among the options. It is NOT that the hospital leads: on the real index the platform is the only exact match at 1.000 and the nearest hospital record scores 0.7833, so no reordering promotes it without abandoning exact matching. That is the naming gap pass 10 identified. My first version of this assertion demanded a non-stop leader AND used `offered_near`, which the platform satisfies by sitting 56 m from the hospital — an assertion the wrong answer could pass.

queries.intent: the hospital by its full name
queries.basis: justified reference point

queries.intent: the stop itself — the user said so
queries.basis: pass-12 M5 / pass-13 M6: explicit transport intent must not be abstained away, and the phrase must be the tail of the query. The role assertion admits `station` as well as `stop` — both are transport features and the query asked for one; the location assertion is what keeps it meaningful, since a stop of this name in Raleigh is the wrong answer Tightened after pass-14 M1: a Raleigh bus stop led while a different candidate supplied the proximity. The LEADER must be the nearby one.

queries.intent: the mall in south Durham
queries.basis: justified reference point; Nominatim resolved this to Kenosha, Wisconsin Tightened after pass-14 M1: a 5 km distance check passed a dessert shop 731 m from the mall reference, which is not the mall. The leader's name must contain the mall's name.

queries.intent: the mall by its full name, which begins with a connective
queries.basis: pass-11 H2: stripping 'The' from both ends matched a different record exactly Tightened after pass-14 M1: any leader within 5 km passed.

queries.intent: Research Triangle Park, a district
queries.basis: a MEASURED COVERAGE GAP, not a scoring problem: no place carries the alias RTP and the index holds POIs, not districts. The requirement is therefore negative — it must not confidently return a business whose name merely contains RTP, kilometres away

queries.intent: the district by its full name
queries.basis: same gap; the 35 matching places are businesses situated in it

queries.intent: the airport
queries.basis: pass-12 H4: the car park merged with the airport and resolved confidently as a car park

queries.intent: the airport by name
queries.basis: a car park is a destination in its own right but is not the airport

queries.intent: the market in Carrboro; the locality is part of the name
queries.basis: pass-11 H2: a locality word that belongs to the name must survive. The reference is the town hall, which the market is beside Tightened after pass-14 M3: any nearby candidate passed.

queries.intent: the co-operative grocery in Carrboro
queries.basis: Several branches exist, so ambiguity is acceptable and no single branch is the right answer. Pass-14 M3 showed the previous 5 km-from-Carrboro assertion would REJECT a correct Hillsborough or Raleigh branch — an assertion no correct answer can pass is as bad as one a wrong answer can. Identity only.

queries.intent: the Carrboro branch of a chain with many branches
queries.basis: pass-9: locality was a score bonus that min(1.0, ...) erased, so this tied four exact matches and the Carrboro shop was not in the top four Tightened after pass-14 M3: locality_match alone does not establish brand identity.

queries.intent: a chain with many branches and no locality given
queries.basis: the Morganton failure mode is auto-picking one of several. Ambiguity is the correct answer

queries.intent: a chain with branches in Chapel Hill and Durham
queries.basis: decision: ambiguity is surfaced, never resolved silently

queries.intent: the Durham branch
queries.basis: pass-10 H2: a LEADING locality sent this to the Amtrak station at 0.85 Tightened after pass-14 M3: a wrong business with locality_match satisfied this.

queries.intent: the Durham branch, locality first
queries.basis: pass-10 H2, the exact form that failed

queries.intent: the Durham branch, with filler words
queries.basis: pass-11 H2: a leading 'the' is filler here and part of the name in 'The Streets At Southpoint', so it has to be a reading rather than a rule

queries.intent: a locality typed with no place name
queries.basis: a bare locality should not confidently return a random business in it

queries.intent: a street, which this index does not hold
queries.basis: streets are addresses, which decision D4 routes to the Census geocoder. The requirement is negative: do not confidently return something far away

queries.intent: the university campus in Raleigh
queries.basis: justified reference point; a campus, so the same district gap as RTP applies

queries.intent: the town north-west of Durham
queries.basis: justified reference point. Note Hillsborough NC and Hillsborough Street in Raleigh both exist, so confident selection of the latter would be wrong

queries.intent: the street in Raleigh, not the town
queries.basis: the discriminating pair for the entry above: the street runs past NC State

queries.intent: the town
queries.basis: justified reference point

queries.intent: a town 180 km outside the metro
queries.basis: THE failure that decided the metro bound. Anything outside the routing bbox is not in the index, so this must not resolve confidently to a local business whose name contains it

queries.intent: a city 300 km outside the metro
queries.basis: the metro bound, from the other side of the state

queries.intent: a chain with a branch in this metro
queries.basis: a grocery query of the kind the product is actually for; the assertion is identity, not location Tightened after pass-14 M3: an unrelated facility passed.

queries.intent: a chain, apostrophe omitted
queries.basis: normalise() folds punctuation, so the apostrophe must not matter Tightened after pass-14 M3: returning the same WRONG facility for both spellings satisfied same_lead_as.

queries.intent: the same chain, apostrophe present
queries.basis: the pair is the test: punctuation must not change the answer

queries.intent: a street whose name is also an institution's
queries.basis: 'Duke' as a street name must not pull the hospital or a campus stop

queries.intent: the transit station in Durham — a station IS a destination
queries.basis: pass-11 M1 and pass-13 M7: station/train_station/halt are one role and a station is not a platform Tightened after pass-14 M3: an unrelated facility passed.

queries.intent: the station, explicit transport phrase
queries.basis: pass-13 M6: an explicit transport phrase at the tail of the query is intent, and the phrase-free form is a further reading so the words do not inflate candidates whose NAMES contain them. pass-14 M1 then showed this resolved CONFIDENTLY to a place named 'Train Station' 32 km away in Raleigh; a typed locality must now be confirmed for confidence, so it is correctly ambiguous. KNOWN RANKING LIMIT, recorded not hidden: the Raleigh record still LEADS, because it matches the locality-stripped reading exactly at 1.000 while 'Durham Station' matches partially, and locality breaks ties rather than outranking score. Demanding the right leader would be an assertion no correct answer can pass today, which is as bad as one a wrong answer can. So this asserts the contract for ambiguity: abstain, and OFFER the right place — pinned to a candidate named 'Durham ... Station' near downtown Durham, so an unrelated business cannot satisfy it.

queries.intent: whatever is named this — the point is that 'bay' is not transport intent
queries.basis: pass-13 M6: a bus stop named 'Bay Leaf Indian Cuisine' suppressed the abstention and won confidently because 'bay' was in the intent word list

queries.intent: a generic fixture word; nothing should be confidently returned
queries.basis: pass-10 H4: a bank merged with its own ATM 9 m away. A generic fixture noun is not a place

queries.intent: a generic word
queries.basis: KNOWN OPEN FAILURE, cause named: a single Overture listing named exactly 'Parking' is the sole exact match at 1.000 and wins outright. Unlike a bare locality, this index CAN hold car parks, so the honest fix is to route a bare category noun to the category criterion rather than to the anchor resolver — a product-routing decision, not a scoring tweak, so it is recorded rather than guessed at. Left red deliberately.

queries.intent: a district
queries.basis: justified reference point; the district gap again

queries.intent: a bare locality that is also part of many names
queries.basis: pass-11 H2 and pass-13 M5 both involved 'Durham' appearing as both locality and name token

queries.intent: nothing typed
queries.basis: an empty query must not be an error and must not return a candidate Tightened after pass-14 M3: a malformed not_found carrying garbage candidates passed.

queries.intent: nonsense
queries.basis: below SCORE_FLOOR nothing is worth showing Tightened after pass-14 M3.

queries.intent: merge tripwire: a chain present in both sources must still corroborate
queries.basis: pass-14 M2: Codex reverted each historical merge over-correction in memory and found that three of four turned NO benchmark assertion red — the unit tests catch them, the benchmark did not. This is a tripwire on real data: if a merge rule regresses, cross-source clusters come apart and the corroborated count drops. The baseline was measured, not assumed.
